headline: Profit swings positive as returns to shareholders climb
summary_short: Chord Energy's Q2 2026 net income swung to $525.2M ($9.28 diluted EPS) from a year-ago loss, as oil volumes of 165.4 MBopd hit the high end of guidance and Adjusted Free Cash Flow rose to $413.4M; the company returned 54% of that FCF via dividends and buybacks.
summary_long: Revenue rose 84% y/y to $2.17B as crude prices recovered from 2Q25's crash and purchased oil-and-gas sales grew with volumes. Net income swung to $525.2M ($9.28 diluted EPS) from a $389.9M loss a year earlier, when a $541.9M non-cash goodwill impairment hit results; Adjusted EBITDA rose 69% to $923.5M and Adjusted Free Cash Flow rose to $413.4M. Chord returned 54% of FCF via a $1.30/share dividend and $147.4M of buybacks, and expects to lift returns to 75% of FCF in Q3 as leverage fell below 0.5x. FY26 guidance held oil-volume and capex midpoints unchanged; LOE guidance was raised on added workover activity and higher non-operated costs. Cash rose to $611.6M against $1.48B long-term debt.

drivers.explanation: 2Q26 oil volumes of 165.4 MBopd were at the high end of guidance, CapEx of $416.7M was modestly below midpoint, and Chord returned 54% of Adjusted FCF via dividends and buybacks; returns are expected to rise to 75% in 3Q26 as leverage fell below half a turn.

Revenue rose on higher realized crude prices ($93.99/bbl vs $61.62/bbl a year earlier) and higher purchased oil-and-gas sales, which move with the volumes Chord buys and resells in its marketing business.
This expense line scales with the matching purchased oil-and-gas revenue in the marketing/trading business and moved in step with it; it is not a core production cost.
The swing to operating income from a loss mainly reflects the absence of the prior-year period's $541.9M non-cash goodwill impairment, plus higher revenue on higher realized oil prices.

The swing to net income follows the operating-income recovery plus a $107.9M net gain on derivative instruments (vs $82.2M a year earlier), partly offset by higher income tax expense as pretax income rose.
Cash built to $611.6M as $1,116.2M of quarterly operating cash flow outpaced $416.7M of CapEx, $147.4M of buybacks, and dividend payments during the quarter.

FY26 oil-volume and CapEx midpoint guidance held unchanged from the May 5 guidance; LOE midpoint guidance was raised to $10.30/BOE on added chemical-workover activity, higher workover costs, and higher non-operated LOE; production-tax guidance ticked up on higher oil-revenue mix.
